items.summary: Kitco AM (sáng thứ Ba 10/11 giờ Mỹ): spot vàng quanh 4.055,30 USD, giảm 84,10 USD (−2,03%); bạc quanh 51,70 USD (−3,01%). CPI tháng 10 tăng 0,4% (dự báo 0,3%; tháng 9 +0,6%), CPI lõi +0,3% (dự báo 0,2%) – lõi đã tăng 0,3% ba tháng liền. Lợi suất 10 năm lên ~4,94%, 2 năm ~4,69%, USD mạnh lên. items.title_en: Spot gold drops ~2% to near $4,055 after hotter October CPI; 10-year yield climbs to ~4.94%
items.summary_en: Kitco AM, early U.S. trading Tuesday: spot gold near $4,055.30, down $84.10 (−2.03%); spot silver near $51.70 (−3.01%). October CPI rose 0.4% (consensus 0.3%; September +0.6%) and core CPI 0.3% (consensus 0.2%), the third straight 0.3% core print. The 10-year yield climbed toward 4.94%, the 2-year toward 4.69%, and the dollar firmed. Per Kitco, futures priced about an 84% chance of a 25 bp hike at the Dec. 8–9 meeting before the release; after CPI and Waller's remarks a quarter-point move was almost fully priced, with some probability on a larger one.
items.reason_en: Near term: sticky 0.3% core inflation lifted yields and the dollar and stalled gold's post-election bounce; Kitco flags support at $4,051.45 then $4,021.85, resistance at $4,088.51 and $4,147.62. Bigger picture: further Fed tightening is a heavy headwind for bullion; Friday's PPI is the next inflation test.

items.title: Waller: cân nhắc tăng 50 điểm cơ bản tháng 12 nếu lạm phát lõi vẫn ~0,3%; Logan: cần ít nhất hai đợt tăng 25 điểm nữa
items.summary: Kitco: Thống đốc Fed Waller nói ông nghiêng về tăng 25 điểm cơ bản ở cuộc họp tháng 12, nhưng nếu CPI tháng 10 có lõi quanh 0,3% hoặc cao hơn thì nên cân nhắc tăng 50 điểm – 'chỉ tăng 25 điểm sẽ đặt uy tín của chúng ta vào rủi ro'. Chủ tịch Fed Dallas Logan cho rằng FOMC cần ít nhất hai đợt tăng 25 điểm nữa, và có thể tăng nhanh hơn trong mùa đông này. CPI sau đó vượt dự báo, đúng điều kiện Waller nêu.
items.reason: Ngắn hạn: tín hiệu diều hâu từ hai quan chức Fed củng cố lợi suất và USD, đè lên vàng. Dài hạn: nếu lộ trình tăng lãi kéo dài sang 2027, sức hút của vàng – tài sản không sinh lãi – tiếp tục bị thử thách; hãy theo dõi PPI thứ Sáu và các phát biểu Fed tiếp theo.

items.title_en: Fed's Waller and Logan signal readiness to hike higher and faster, with 50 bps on the table for December
items.summary_en: Kitco: Fed Governor Waller said he leans toward a 25 bp hike in December but that if October core CPI ran around 0.3% or higher, a 50 bp hike should be considered — 'Hiking only 25 basis points would put our credibility at risk.' Dallas Fed's Logan said the FOMC needs at least two more 25 bp increases and may be able to move faster this winter. CPI then printed above consensus, the condition Waller flagged.
items.reason_en: Near term: hawkish signals from two Fed officials reinforce yields and the dollar, weighing on gold. Bigger picture: if the hiking path stretches into 2027, non-yielding gold stays under pressure; watch Friday's PPI and further Fed speakers.

items.title_en: Spot gold holds the rebound: Kitco PM ~$4,087.26 (+0.64%); session high ~$4,148 — softer yields, tech-led Wall Street plunge
items.summary_en: Kitco’s PM wrap Thursday: spot gold near $4,087.26 (+$25.93, +0.64%) and silver near $51.778 (−$0.407, −0.78%). Session high ~$4,148 — highest since Oct. 20. CNBC: spot +1% at $4,100.27 by 2:05 PM ET after a high of $4,146.63; December COMEX futures settled +1% at $4,113.50. Drivers: the 10-year eased toward ~4.82%–4.84%, the dollar index hovered near 101.57 after Wednesday’s drop, and equities cratered (S&P 500 −4.36%, Nasdaq ~−5.5%) on an AI/chip washout — defensive flows helped bullion. December hike odds fell sharply (Investing.com 60.3%).
items.reason_en: Near term: gold kept most of the post-election bounce on lower yields and softer December hike odds — but silver’s fade shows industrial/tech liquidation still bites. Bigger picture: Friday’s NFP (est. ~59k–65k) and oil’s rebound toward $100 can reprice yields fast. Holding above Kitco’s ~$4,075 support is the first test that the recovery sticks toward $4,146–$4,212 resistance.

items.title: Brent +3,8% chốt 98,29 USD; WTI +2,7% về 90,52 – tanker Hormuz bị tấn; Eurasia hạ xác suất deal Iran xuống 10%
items.summary: CNBC/Kitco: Brent futures +3,8% chốt 98,29 USD/thùng; WTI +2,7% chốt 90,52 – lấy lại một phần cú −8%+ hôm trước. Động lực: tấn công tàu chở dầu quanh Hormuz (UKMTO: ít nhất 5 vụ từ Chủ nhật; Iran tuyên bố nhiều tàu/tàu kéo hỏa hoạn do thủy lôi/đường đi không phép). Qatar vẫn trung gian nhưng chưa có thỏa thuận. Eurasia Group: xác suất đòn Mỹ mới 60% (từ 65%), deal 10% (từ 20%), bế tắc kéo dài 30% (từ 15%); nếu leo thang Brent có thể về 110–125. Citi cảnh báo Nhà Trắng có thể dùng quyền hành pháp đẩy chiến tranh sau bầu cử.
items.reason: Ngắn hạn: dầu hồi → tái áp lực lạm phát năng lượng, có thể hạn chế đà vàng nếu lợi suất bật lại; mặt khác bất ổn Hormuz vẫn đỡ nhu cầu trú ẩn. Dài hạn: chưa có deal Hormuz; Quốc hội Dân chủ từ tháng 1 mới siết ngân sách chiến tranh. Mọi tin xấu Iran có thể đẩy Brent và cửa tăng lãi Fed lên lại.

items.title_en: Brent +3.8% settles at $98.29; WTI +2.7% at $90.52 — Hormuz tanker hits; Eurasia cuts Iran deal odds to 10%
items.summary_en: CNBC/Kitco: Brent futures rose 3.8% to settle at $98.29/bbl; WTI +2.7% to $90.52 — clawing back part of Wednesday’s 8%+ collapse. The driver: fresh tanker attacks around Hormuz (UKMTO: at least five vessel incidents since Sunday; Iran claimed multiple ships/a tug caught fire after unauthorized routes/mines). Qatar is still mediating with no deal. Eurasia Group: chance of renewed U.S. strikes 60% (from 65%), a deal 10% (from 20%), prolonged standoff 30% (from 15%); escalation could push Brent toward $110–$125. Citi flagged the White House may lean on executive powers to escalate after the midterms.
items.reason_en: Near term: oil’s rebound reloads energy-inflation pressure — that can cap gold if yields bounce; Hormuz chaos still feeds safe-haven demand. Longer term: still no Hormuz deal; a Democratic Congress only seats in January. Any Iran setback can reprice Brent and December hike odds higher again.

items.summary_en: BLS/CNBC/Reuters: initial jobless claims fell 6,000 to a seasonally adjusted 189,000 for the week ended Oct. 31 (Reuters est. ~196,000 / Dow Jones ~197,000) — matching the mid-July trough, the lowest since around 1969. Four-week average ~194,750; continuing claims ~1.718 million. Nonfarm productivity rose at a 3.6% annualized pace in Q3 (est. ~2.8%); unit labor costs −0.7%. Investing.com Fed Rate Monitor (CME futures), 6:15 PM ET Nov 5: Dec. 9 — hold 39.7% (prior day 18.5%); hike to 4.00%–4.25% 60.3% (prior day 81.5%). Jan. 27, 2027: hold 33.1%; 4.00%–4.25% 56.9%; 4.25%–4.50% 10.1%. Cleveland Fed’s Hammack: policy needs to move more restrictive to get inflation back to 2%; she prefers more frequent, smaller steps. Richmond’s Barkin: a gradual hike pace “makes sense.” Markets await October NFP Friday 8:30 AM ET — Dow Jones ~59,000 / Reuters ~65,000; unemployment ~4.2%.
items.reason_en: Near term: December hike odds crashing from ~82% to ~60% is the clearest gold tailwind of the session — even with firm claims and a still-hawkish Hammack. Bigger picture: Friday’s payrolls/wages decide it. A hot print can re-spike hike odds and yields and clip the $4,100–$4,150 bounce; a soft one cements the hold path and opens a clean test of higher resistance.

items.summary: CNBC/Kitco: WTI mất 8,3% chốt 88,12 USD/thùng; Brent −8,7% chốt 94,62 – mức thấp nhất khoảng 2 tháng. Đảng Dân chủ thắng lưỡng viện → kỳ vọng Quốc hội siết ngân sách chiến tranh và ép hạ nhiệt xung đột Hormuz. Dầu đã giảm hơn 14% trong tuần khi Mỹ–Iran mở cửa ngoại giao; Qatar vẫn trung gian. items.reason: Ngắn hạn: dầu lao dốc → bớt áp lực lạm phát năng lượng → hỗ trợ vàng qua kênh lợi suất kỳ vọng. Dài hạn: chưa có thỏa thuận Hormuz; đòn Mỹ gần đây và tấn công tàu vẫn giữ rủi ro nguồn cung. Mọi tin xấu Iran có thể đẩy Brent và xác suất tăng lãi Fed lên lại.

items.title_en: WTI −8.3% settles at $88.12; Brent −8.7% at $94.62 — Vance blames Iran war for GOP midterm losses, market prices de-escalation
items.summary_en: CNBC/Kitco: WTI lost 8.3% to settle at $88.12/bbl; Brent shed 8.7% to $94.62 — about a two-month low. VP JD Vance posted that “the reason we lost is the war”; Trump also tied gasoline/Iran to the midterm rout. Democrats’ dual-chamber win raised bets that Congress will squeeze war funding and push a Hormuz off-ramp. Crude is down more than 14% this week on U.S.–Iran deal chatter; Qatar is still mediating. CIBC’s Babin warned the selloff may be overdone; Rapidan’s McNally still leans escalation risk.
items.reason_en: Near term: plunging oil eases energy-inflation pressure — that helps gold via lower expected yields. Longer term: there is still no Hormuz deal; recent U.S. strikes and ship attacks keep supply risk alive. Any Iran setback can reprice Brent and December hike odds higher again, and that would cap bullion.

items.title_en: Brent settles −1.1% at $103.60, WTI −0.4% at $96.09 — Qatar still mediating; Iran rejects “coercion” diplomacy; U.S. hit Qeshm Island
items.summary_en: CNBC/Kitco: Brent futures settled $1.17 (−1.1%) at $103.60/bbl; WTI lost $0.37 (−0.4%) to $96.09 — a second down day after Monday’s 7% slide. The driver: deal chatter. Qatar’s Foreign Ministry said a delegation met Tehran and both sides are reviewing mediator proposals. Iran’s FM spokesman Baqaei (IRNA): Tehran will not accept diplomacy based on coercion. WSJ via CNBC: the U.S. struck Iran’s Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz on Monday — officials called it a limited, defensive action. UKMTO: at least four ship attacks since the start of the month. Aramco’s CEO: Hormuz flows remain below pre-conflict levels.
items.reason_en: Near term: softer oil eases energy-inflation pressure — that would help gold if yields weren’t rising. Longer term: there is still no deal; Iranian officials say one remains distant; the Qeshm strike and ship attacks keep supply risk alive. Any Hormuz setback can reprice Brent and December hike odds higher again, and that would cap bullion.

Longer term: a divided Congress could curb new spending/tax bills and ease long-end issuance pressure (gold-friendly), but only if the labor data doesn’t lock in a December hike.

items.title_en: Gold rebounds 1.8% to ~$3,944–$3,946 from a one-year low; silver climbs 2.9%–3.7% back above $50 as oil’s slide does the heavy lifting
items.summary_en: CNBC: spot gold rose 1.8% to $3,943.62/oz at 2:54 p.m. ET Monday, after Friday’s 3.6% drop that marked the lowest since October 2025. December COMEX futures settled 1.8% higher at $3,969.60. Kitco’s PM wrap had spot near $3,945.80 (+$71.40, +1.84%) and silver near $50.80 (+$1.80, +3.67%). Gold’s 14-day RSI lifted to about 37 from below 30 on Friday — out of technically oversold territory. Zaner Metals’ Peter Grant: softer oil is easing inflation worries, though the market still leans toward a December Fed hike even as those odds have edged down from last week.
items.reason_en: Near term: this is a technical bounce after the month-end flush, helped by oil’s 7% slide and a softer dollar/yields backdrop — not a trend flip yet. Kitco maps resistance at $3,978 then $4,035; support at $3,817 then $3,719. Bigger picture: bullion is still roughly 28%–30% below January’s ~$5,600 peak. Julius Baer’s Carsten Menke argues U.S. deficits persist whatever the midterms bring, so the debt/interest burden remains a longer-term gold support — but a ~73%–75% December hike probability is still the main near-term lid.

items.title_en: Brent settles −7.6% at $104.77, WTI −7.4% at $96.46 — no Iran deal yet, but Trump says one “could happen”
items.summary_en: Reuters: Brent futures settled $8.66 (−7.63%) at $104.77/bbl; WTI dropped $7.66 (−7.36%) to $96.46 — Kitco called it the largest daily percentage decline for both since July. The move followed Iranian President Pezeshkian saying the Supreme Leader had granted the government “certain authorities” for talks; Trump said Iran wants a deal and that one “could happen”; Qatari mediators flew to Tehran Monday evening to meet Foreign Minister Araqchi. Tehran says its seven-step plan has been condensed and could be implemented in two days (reopening Hormuz if the U.S. lifts its port blockade). Reuters: Doha talks ended without a breakthrough; Iranian sources still see a fresh U.S. strike as more likely than a deal.
items.reason_en: Near term: the oil dump eases energy-inflation fears — that helped gold bounce and took some heat out of yields and the dollar. Longer term: there is still no signed deal. Raymond James’ Molchanov flags many “false dawns”; Goldman Sachs still sketches Brent at $140 in 2027 if Gulf output stays ~3.5 mb/d below the 2025 average. Any Hormuz setback can reprice oil and hike odds higher again, and that would cap gold.

items.summary: Kitco: thứ Sáu 30/10 vàng giao ngay rơi 3,52–3,62% trong phiên, chốt tuần quanh 3.875 USD (−3,74% cả tuần), đáy tuần 3.870,25 – thấp nhất hơn một năm theo Kitco. Đỉnh tuần 4.082,50 lập ngay trước khi Fed ra quyết định. Bạc mất khoảng 6% còn ~49 USD, lần đầu dưới 50 USD sau 11 tháng. Nguyên nhân chính: Nasdaq giảm 2,86% vì lo chi tiêu AI không sinh lời, kéo theo dòng bán thanh lý và gọi ký quỹ trên kim loại quý (Commerzbank, trader Tai Wong). Reuters: vàng hướng tới tháng giảm thứ hai liên tiếp. Đầu phiên Á sáng 2/11 (fx678): vàng giao ngay quanh 3.892 USD rồi đứng lại trên 3.900 USD, tăng khoảng 0,5–0,7%.
items.reason: Ngắn hạn: nhịp hồi sáng nay là hồi kỹ thuật sau cú xả cuối tháng, chưa đổi xu hướng. Kitco: cản 3.890–3.910 rồi 3.943, 3.975; hỗ trợ 3.800 rồi 3.780 – còn dưới 3.910 thì phe bán vẫn cầm trịch. Điều đáng chú ý là lợi suất và USD giảm mà vàng vẫn rơi: khi cổ phiếu bị bán mạnh, vàng bị bán theo để lấy tiền mặt. Dài hạn: vàng đã mất khoảng 30% từ đỉnh 5.595 USD tháng 1; dưới 4.000 thường kéo ngân hàng trung ương vào mua, nhưng chừng nào Fed còn nghiêng tăng lãi thì lực hồi khó bền.

items.title_en: Gold drops 3.7% on the week to ~$3,875 as the tech rout forces liquidation – a modest bounce back to $3,900 at the Sunday open
items.summary_en: Kitco: spot gold lost 3.5%–3.6% on Friday and finished the week near $3,875 (−3.74% w/w), with a weekly low of $3,870.25 – Kitco's weakest print in more than a year. The weekly high of $4,082.50 came right before the Fed decision. Silver shed about 6% to roughly $49, below $50 for the first time in 11 months. The trigger was a 2.86% slide in the Nasdaq on doubts about AI spending returns, which spilled into forced selling and margin calls across precious metals (Commerzbank, independent trader Tai Wong). Reuters: bullion is headed for a second straight monthly loss. In early Asian trade (fx678), spot traded near $3,892 before reclaiming $3,900, up roughly 0.5%–0.7%.
items.reason_en: Near term: the Sunday-night pop is a technical bounce off a month-end flush, not a trend change. Kitco maps resistance at $3,890–$3,910, then $3,943 and $3,975; support at $3,800, then $3,780 – as long as price stays under $3,910, sellers are in control. The tell is that gold fell even as yields and the dollar eased: when equities get hit this hard, gold gets sold to raise cash. Bigger picture: bullion is down about 30% from January's $5,595 record; sub-$4,000 prices tend to draw central-bank buying, but with the Fed still leaning toward a hike, rallies are hard to sustain.

items.title: Iran – Qatar đàm phán ngày thứ ba ở Doha về kế hoạch mở lại Hormuz trong 2 ngày – Brent đầu tuần lùi hơn 1% về 111,9 USD
items.summary: CNBC (Reuters, 20:30 VN 1/11): đoàn Iran họp ngày thứ ba liên tiếp với trung gian Qatar tại Doha nhằm chấm dứt chiến tranh Mỹ – Israel với Iran. Ngoại trưởng Araqchi nói thảo luận về «kế hoạch hai ngày» – mở lại eo Hormuz trong 2 ngày nếu đạt thỏa thuận với Washington – «đang tiến triển» nhưng chưa có kết luận. Ông Trump nói Mỹ sẽ không tấn công Iran trước bầu cử giữa kỳ 3/11 nhưng không loại trừ hành động sau đó. Thứ Sáu, một tàu chở dầu ở Hormuz trúng mìn gắn thân tàu; Brent kỳ hạn tháng 12 chốt 117,64 USD (+2,4%), cao nhất từ cuối tháng 4, WTI 104,12 USD; cả tháng Brent +13,6%. OPEC+ giữ nguyên sản lượng tháng 12 (CNBC 1/11). Reuters 06:03 VN 2/11: Brent −1,33% còn 111,92 USD, WTI −1,71% còn 102,34 USD.
items.reason: Ngắn hạn: dầu hạ nhờ hy vọng đàm phán giúp giảm bớt nỗi lo lạm phát và áp lực Fed tăng lãi – hỗ trợ nhẹ cho nhịp hồi của vàng. Nhưng rủi ro lớn nằm sau ngày 3/11: nếu Mỹ quay lại tấn công, dầu tăng vọt sẽ đẩy cược tăng lãi lên và vàng lại bị ép, như đã thấy suốt tháng 10. Dài hạn: dầu trên 100 USD kéo dài giữ lạm phát cao, lãi suất cao lâu hơn – bất lợi cho vàng; một thỏa thuận mở lại Hormuz thật sự mới là yếu tố đổi chiều.

items.title_en: Iran and Qatar hold a third day of talks on a two-day plan to reopen Hormuz – Brent slips more than 1% to $111.92 at the open
items.summary_en: CNBC (Reuters): Iranian negotiators met Qatari mediators in Doha for a third straight day on Sunday, pushing for a deal to end the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran. Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi said talks on a "two-day proposal" – reopening the Strait of Hormuz within two days of an agreement with Washington – are "ongoing and progressing," with no final conclusion. President Trump has said the U.S. won't launch new strikes before Tuesday's midterms but hasn't ruled out action afterward. On Friday a tanker in the strait was hit by limpet mines; December Brent settled at $117.64 (+2.4%), its highest since late April, and WTI at $104.12, with Brent up 13.6% in October. OPEC+ left December output targets unchanged. Reuters at 6:03 PM ET Sunday: Brent −1.33% to $111.92, WTI −1.71% to $102.34.
items.reason_en: Near term: crude backing off on diplomacy takes a little heat out of the inflation story and the hike odds, which gives gold some room to bounce. The real risk sits after Nov 3 – if strikes resume, an oil spike lifts hike bets and squeezes gold again, the same pattern we saw all October. Longer term: $100-plus crude keeps inflation sticky and rates higher for longer, which is a headwind for gold; only an actual deal that reopens Hormuz changes that.

items.title_en: 10-year yield ends the week at 4.93%–4.94%, a roughly 7-week low, with the dollar flat near 102 – gold gets no help
items.summary_en: Stocktwits/BondStats: the 10-year Treasury yield closed the week at 4.93%–4.94% (−4 bps Friday, −7 bps w/w), the 2-year at 4.56%–4.59% (down about 10 bps on the week), and the 30-year was little changed at 5.31%–5.32%. Money rotated out of AI names (the SOX fell 7.2% Friday) and into duration. The Dollar Index settled at 101.96–101.97, flat on the week (+0.08% Friday).
items.reason_en: Near term: falling yields are usually a tailwind for gold, but last week the safety bid went into Treasuries, not bullion – gold was sold to cover equity losses. Once the equity selling calms down, lower yields can help a bounce. Longer term: the 10-year real yield is still around 2.6%, which keeps the opportunity cost of holding gold high until the Fed turns.

items.title_en: Pivotal week: Tuesday's midterms and Friday's 8:30 AM ET payrolls – FedWatch prices about 72% odds of a December hike
items.summary_en: CME FedWatch (via FXBus, late Oct 30): 72% odds of a 25-bp hike at the Dec 8–9 meeting vs. 28% for a hold; by January 2027, 58.4% for a cumulative 25 bps and 22.3% for 50 bps. The calendar (FXStreet/XM): ISM manufacturing Monday at 10:00 AM ET; midterm elections Tuesday (Democrats favored to take the House, the Senate a toss-up); ADP and ISM services Wednesday; RBA (Tuesday) and BoE (Thursday) both expected to hike; October nonfarm payrolls Friday at 8:30 AM ET after September's weak +29,000. Earnings: Apple and Palantir Monday, AMD Tuesday, Qualcomm Wednesday. The Oct 28 FOMC held at 3.75%–4.00% with two dissents (Cook, Hammack) for an immediate hike.
items.reason_en: Near term: payrolls are the main test – a strong print could lock in December and push gold lower; another soft number like September's opens the door to a relief rally. Midterms: a Republican sweep likely lifts the dollar and yields on tariff and inflation worries, a negative for gold, while a split Congress tends to cool the dollar. And once the vote is done, the risk of renewed U.S. strikes on Iran comes back into play. Longer term: markets price the fed funds rate roughly 70 bps higher by the end of 2027 – nothing yet argues for a turn in gold's bigger trend.

items.title: Musalem đòi tăng lãi «sớm», Daly bàn AI, Barkin muốn từ từ – Fed nghiêng diều hâu, vàng đi ngang quanh 3.900 USD
items.summary: Musalem (Fed St. Louis, 23:30 VN, CNBC/Reuters): «Tôi đánh giá việc thắt chặt thêm sẽ cần thiết, và sớm»; «điều chỉnh từng bước sớm thường ít gây xáo trộn hơn hành động lớn, đột ngột về sau»; lạm phát «quá cao», kinh tế «vững». Daly (Fed San Francisco, 23:00 VN, investingLive): AI quan trọng với chính sách trong ngắn và trung hạn, liên quan cả hai nhiệm vụ giá cả và việc làm – không gợi ý lãi suất. Barkin (Fed Richmond, 20:30 VN, Bloomberg qua Yahoo Finance): hướng đi «rõ ràng», chỉ còn tốc độ, «đi từ từ là cách tốt»; đầu tư AI đang đẩy lạm phát phía cầu. So với dự đoán: Musalem diều hâu – đúng; Daly trung lập – đúng. Thị trường gần như không phản ứng: vàng giao ngay quanh 3.899 USD lúc 12:32 ET (Why Gold Moved), HĐ vàng tháng 12 đi ngang 3.905–3.910 USD trong lúc phát biểu (Yahoo Finance); DXY ~101,9; lợi suất 10 năm ~4,95% (−4 điểm cơ bản trong ngày). CME FedWatch ~75% tăng lãi tháng 12 (FXStreet).
items.reason: Hawkish đã nằm sẵn trong giá: vàng mất gần 3% từ trước giờ phát biểu, nên Musalem chỉ xác nhận chứ không tạo cú rơi mới. Kế hoạch giữ nguyên: chưa bắt đáy khi giá còn dưới 3.950–4.000, ưu tiên bán hồi; thủng 3.890 thì mở đường về 3.850. Cook và Hammack (2 người phản đối, muốn tăng lãi) chưa có bài giải thích công khai – cần theo dõi. Làm theo kế hoạch, đừng chạy theo nến tin.

items.title_en: Musalem wants a hike 'soon,' Daly talks AI, Barkin prefers gradual – Fed leans hawkish, gold flat near $3,900
items.summary_en: Musalem (St. Louis Fed, 12:30 PM ET, CNBC/Reuters): "I judge that additional firming of monetary policy will be necessary, and soon"; "incremental adjustments made earlier are usually less disruptive than larger and abrupt actions taken later"; inflation is "too high," the economy "resilient." Daly (San Francisco Fed, noon ET, investingLive): AI matters for policy in the near and medium term, for both the price-stability and employment mandates — no rate signal. Barkin (Richmond Fed, 9:30 AM ET radio, Bloomberg via Yahoo Finance): direction of travel is "straightforward," the question is pace, and "a gradual approach is a good way to go"; AI investment is fueling demand-side inflation. Versus our call: Musalem hawkish — right; Daly neutral — right. Market barely moved: spot gold near $3,899 at 12:32 PM ET (Why Gold Moved), December futures flat at $3,905–$3,910 through the remarks (Yahoo Finance); DXY ~101.9; 10-year yield ~4.95% (down 4 bps on the day). CME FedWatch ~75% odds of a December hike (FXStreet).
items.reason_en: The hawkish message was already in the price — gold had dropped nearly 3% before anyone spoke, so Musalem confirmed rather than triggered. The plan doesn't change: no bottom-fishing while price sits below $3,950–$4,000, favor selling bounces, and a break of $3,890 opens $3,850. The two hawkish dissenters, Cook and Hammack, haven't published their explanations yet — worth watching. Trade the plan, not the noise.

items.summary_en: BEA/CNBC: third-quarter GDP grew at a 3.4% annualized pace (consensus 3.1%–3.2%, Q2 2.2%). Initial jobless claims dropped to about 194,000. Kitco had spot gold at $4,024.60 late in New York, down $42.00 (−1.03%), with silver off 3.1% at $52.18, an 11-month low. Most of gold's damage was done in Asia and early London, before the numbers; the print itself got a few dollars of pop that faded right away. CNBC (Reuters): bullion is on track for a second straight monthly loss.
items.reason_en: Near term: a hot economy plus 3.6% inflation keeps a December hike on the table, so gold has no fuel for a durable bounce. Kitco maps resistance at 4,084 then 4,146, support at 4,024 then 3,986 – lose 4,024 and the $4,000 handle and 3,986 come into play. Longer term: energy inflation bleeding into services (core services ex-housing at 3.6% y/y) means higher-for-longer rates, so the intermediate trend still leans lower until inflation clearly turns.

items.title_en: ECB holds at 2.5% but flags a December hike – Lagarde says the 'direction of travel' is clear; markets price ~67%
items.summary_en: The ECB left the deposit rate at 2.50%, the refi rate at 2.65% and the marginal lending rate at 2.90%, warning that rising energy prices skew inflation risks higher and growth risks lower; euro-area inflation is running at 3.8%, the highest since September 2023 (CNBC). Lagarde said the Governing Council debated a hike before choosing to wait for more data, and that barring a major development 'the direction of travel is quite clear.' Reuters sources say a Dec. 17 hike is all but certain, followed by a pause. Money markets price roughly a 67% chance of a December move (LSEG). Lagarde also announced she will step down early.
items.reason_en: Near term: a hawkish ECB lifts the euro and trims the dollar – a modest tailwind for gold. Longer term: major central banks are all leaning toward tightening on the energy shock, and a higher global rate floor remains a shared headwind for bullion.

items.title_en: Fed holds at 3.75%–4.00% on a 10–2 vote – Cook and Hammack dissent for a hike, Warsh won't pre-commit on December
items.summary_en: The FOMC left the funds rate at 3.75%–4.00%, as expected, but Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack both dissented in favor of a quarter-point hike. The statement upgraded growth to a "strong pace," said inflation "remains elevated" and that the "accumulation of more information" will guide the next move. At the presser, Chair Kevin Warsh refused to prejudge December, saying the Fed has "made clear our readiness to act," and announced that one 2027 meeting will be strategy-only, with no rate vote. CNBC called Cook's dissent the real stunner – her first since joining the Board in 2022.
items.reason_en: Near term: a hold with two hawkish dissents keeps a December hike priced at roughly 82%–86%, so gold lacks a catalyst to break out and rallies into 4,080–4,100 are likely to be sold. Longer term: a Fed still leaning toward tightening into a fast-growing economy keeps real rates high – the biggest headwind for bullion until inflation clearly rolls over.

items.title_en: Crude slides for a second day – Brent $114.80, WTI $100.88 – as Tehran talks revive hopes of cooling the U.S.-Iran war
items.summary_en: CNBC: by 1:09 AM ET, Brent was down 0.87% at $114.80 a barrel and WTI down 0.86% at $100.88 after Saudi, Turkish and Pakistani officials met Iranian leaders in Tehran and agreed to keep talking. President Trump says he's close to deciding between a deal with Iran and stepped-up military action. The drop is capped by ongoing Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, and October has been the worst month for shipping attacks around the Strait of Hormuz.
items.reason_en: Near term: cooler crude eases the inflation scare, but not enough to pull yields or the dollar lower – so gold isn't getting the benefit. A bad Hormuz or Houthi headline could send oil right back up. Longer term: the war is still live – an inflation risk that hurts gold through rates, but also a haven bid on any surprise escalation.

items.title_en: Crude settles lower – Brent $115.81, WTI $101.76 – as Saudi defense chief meets Iran's president, but Houthi strikes continue and the SPR sits at a 1982 low
items.summary_en: CNBC: Brent lost 91 cents to settle at $115.81 after briefly topping $117; WTI fell $1.51 to $101.76. Crude is still up about 12% this month. Saudi Defense Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian in Tehran, with Pakistani and Turkish officials attending. Per Reuters, the Houthis claimed hits on pumping stations along Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, and Egypt's parliament authorized President el-Sisi to take "all necessary measures" to help defend the kingdom. The Strategic Petroleum Reserve fell to 282.6 million barrels, the lowest since October 1982.
items.reason_en: Near term: Saudi-Iran talks take some heat out of crude, easing the inflation and yield pressure that's been capping gold. Longer term: the war premium is still baked into oil and a depleted SPR limits Washington's ability to cap prices – one successful strike on Saudi infrastructure sends crude and yields higher and puts gold back on the defensive.

items.title_en: 10-year yield flat at 4.987% while the 2-year climbs to 4.712% after a soft $69 billion auction; Deutsche Bank still sees a hawkish Fed message
items.summary_en: WSJ: as of 3:46 PM ET, the 10-year yield was unchanged at 4.987%, the 2-year rose 3.2 basis points to 4.712%, and the 30-year slipped 1.4 bps to 5.300%. The $69 billion 2-year auction tailed, a sign of soft demand (BMO). Deutsche Bank, via CNBC, says the message will stay hawkish even with a pause this week, and expects Chair Warsh to stress that tighter financial conditions are no substitute for higher policy rates. Up next: September durable goods (WSJ consensus +1.7%) and Conference Board consumer confidence.
items.reason_en: Near term: a firmer 2-year says the market is still holding its hike bets, which caps gold's bounce; a flat long end means no fresh pressure for now. Longer term: a 10-year near 5% is a steep opportunity cost for a non-yielding asset – the trend in gold won't turn until long yields come down for real.

Dài hạn: Fed vẫn trong chu kỳ thắt chặt khi lạm phát lan rộng; lãi suất thực cao tiếp tục đè vàng cho tới khi lạm phát quay đầu.

items.title_en: Fed set to pause, "but maybe not for long" – inflation is broadening and December hike odds climb to 72.1%
items.summary_en: Reuters: Fed officials have telegraphed no move this week (3.75%–4.00%), but September inflation broadened well beyond fuel, Q3 growth accelerated and unemployment is steady at 4.2%. Nationwide's Kathy Bostjancic says the data support a hike, and that the Fed only blinked because the 10-year spiked toward quarter-century highs after the September move – New York Fed President John Williams and Vice Chair Philip Jefferson both signaled patience. Investing.com's Fed Rate Monitor (CME-based) as of 7:05 PM ET: 89.7% odds of a hold on Wednesday; December hike odds up to 72.1% from 67.6%. The decision is at 2:00 PM ET Wednesday.
items.reason_en: Near term: the hold is priced, so the move comes from the statement and Warsh's presser – if he keeps December live, the dollar and 2-year yields firm and gold struggles to hold $4,000. Longer term: the Fed is still tightening into broadening inflation, and high real rates keep weighing on gold until inflation rolls over.

items.title: Cuối tuần: Ả Rập Xê Út đánh chặn loạt tên lửa, drone Houthi nhắm Riyadh và cơ sở Aramco ở Yanbu; thị trường mở cửa đầu tuần với rủi ro Mỹ – Israel tấn công Iran sau bầu cử giữa kỳ 3/11

Houthi tuyên bố thực hiện «bảy chiến dịch», nhắm sân bay quốc tế King Khalid và cơ sở Aramco ở Yanbu. Chưa có báo cáo thiệt hại hay thương vong; sân bay Riyadh mở lại nhà ga 1 và 2 ngay trong ngày (AP). Phát biểu của Tổng thống Trump tuần trước gợi ý Mỹ và Israel lên kế hoạch tấn công Iran sau bầu cử giữa kỳ 3/11 – yếu tố đã đẩy Brent lên 116,72 USD, cao nhất 6 tháng, hôm thứ Sáu. Các diễn biến cuối tuần chưa được phản ánh vào giá vì thị trường đóng cửa.

Nếu không có thiệt hại thật ở cơ sở dầu, phần bù rủi ro có thể hạ nhiệt và giảm bớt sức ép. Dài hạn: mốc 3/11 là chất xúc tác hai chiều – xung đột lan sang hạ tầng năng lượng sẽ giữ lạm phát cao lâu hơn; hạ nhiệt hoặc đàm phán mới là điều kiện để vàng lấy lại vai trò trú ẩn.

items.title_en: Weekend flare-up: Saudi Arabia knocks down Houthi missiles and drones aimed at Riyadh and Aramco's Yanbu sites as markets reopen with post-midterm Iran strike risk in play
items.summary_en: CNBC: the Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted two drones and a ballistic missile headed for Riyadh, 10 ballistic missiles aimed at the south and a cruise missile targeting Khamis Mushait on Sunday. The Houthis claimed "seven qualitative military operations," naming King Khalid International Airport and Aramco facilities at Yanbu. No damage or casualties were reported, and Riyadh's airport reopened Terminals 1 and 2 the same day (AP). President Trump's remarks last week suggesting the US and Israel are planning fresh strikes on Iran after the Nov. 3 midterms helped push Brent to a six-month high of $116.72 on Friday. None of the weekend news is priced yet.
items.reason_en: Near term: the risk is another leg higher in crude at the open – and right now higher oil means higher inflation expectations and yields, which hurts gold more than any haven bid helps it. If no barrels are actually lost, the risk premium can bleed out and ease the pressure. Longer term: Nov. 3 cuts both ways. Strikes that hit energy infrastructure keep inflation sticky; a de-escalation or a new round of talks is what gold needs to trade like a haven again.

items.title: Tuần FOMC: giới phân tích chờ một «khoảng dừng diều hâu» – thị trường đặt ~90% Fed giữ lãi 28/10 nhưng ~70% tăng 25 điểm cơ bản tháng 12
items.summary: Yahoo Finance: Fed bước vào cuộc họp 27–28/10 với lạm phát nóng hơn – CPI tháng 9 lên 3,7% so với cùng kỳ, giá sản xuất tăng hơn 6%, và PCE lõi dự báo vượt 3%. Cựu Phó Chủ tịch Fed Alan Blinder dự đoán «khoảng dừng diều hâu»: giữ lãi nhưng gợi ý cuộc họp tới có thể tăng. Ken Rogoff (Harvard) cho rằng xét nền tảng thì nên tăng, nhưng Fed sẽ giữ vì bầu cử giữa kỳ chỉ còn chưa đầy một tuần. Cleveland Fed Beth Hammack nghiêng về tăng ngay từng bước nhỏ. Thị trường định giá gần 90% giữ lãi tuần này và 70% tăng 25 điểm cơ bản tháng 12. Quyết định công bố 01:00 VN thứ Năm 29/10, họp báo của Chủ tịch Warsh lúc 01:30 VN.
items.reason: Ngắn hạn: giữ lãi gần như đã được định giá, nên biến động sẽ đến từ câu chữ – nếu Warsh xác nhận cửa tăng tháng 12, lợi suất và USD giữ vững, vàng khó lấy lại 4.000; nếu Fed nhấn mạnh «chờ thêm dữ liệu», vàng có cơ hội hồi kỹ thuật. Dài hạn: Fed vẫn trong chu kỳ thắt chặt khi lạm phát dai dẳng – môi trường lãi suất thực cao là lực cản chính của vàng cho tới khi lạm phát quay đầu.

items.title_en: Fed week: the Street is bracing for a "hawkish pause" – roughly 90% odds of a hold on Oct. 28, but about 70% odds of a quarter-point hike in December
items.summary_en: Yahoo Finance: the Fed heads into its Oct. 27–28 meeting with inflation running hotter – September CPI at 3.7% y/y, wholesale prices up more than 6%, and core PCE projected above 3%. Former Fed Vice Chair Alan Blinder expects a "hawkish pause" that strongly hints the next move could be a hike. Harvard's Ken Rogoff says the fundamentals call for a hike but the Fed will hold with the midterms less than a week away. Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack has argued for small hikes now. Traders price nearly 90% odds of a hold this week and 70% odds of a quarter-point hike in December. The statement is due Wednesday at 2:00 PM ET, with Chair Warsh's presser at 2:30 PM ET.
items.reason_en: Near term: a hold is priced, so the move comes from the wording. If Warsh keeps December firmly on the table, yields and the dollar stay bid and $4,000 stays a ceiling for gold; if the message leans "we need more data," there's room for a relief bounce. Longer term: the Fed is still in a tightening cycle against sticky inflation, and high real rates remain gold's main headwind until inflation rolls over.

items.reason_en: Near term: a weekly close under $4,000 is a bad technical look – $4,000 flips to resistance for Monday, and bulls need it back fast or the selling keeps coming. Đại học Michigan (chốt tháng 10): niềm tin tiêu dùng 48,0 (tháng 9: 48,1); kỳ vọng lạm phát 1 năm 4,7% (từ 4,6%), dài hạn 3,5% (từ 3,4%), đều cao nhất từ tháng 5; 69% người tiêu dùng cho rằng lãi suất sẽ tăng trong năm tới, cao nhất từ 4/2023.
items.reason: Ngắn hạn: giá bán tăng mạnh cùng kỳ vọng lạm phát nhích lên củng cố lập luận Fed tăng lãi tháng 12 – bất lợi cho vàng. Dài hạn: kinh tế Mỹ vẫn nóng (S&P Global ước GDP quý 4 tăng ~5%/năm) nên Fed khó quay lại nới lỏng sớm; vàng chỉ hưởng lợi nếu lạm phát vượt tầm kiểm soát và lãi suất thực giảm.

items.title_en: US flash PMI: selling prices rise fastest since Aug. 2022 (59.8); Michigan 1-year inflation expectations 4.7%, long-run 3.5% – both highest since May
items.summary_en: Reuters (via Investing.com): S&P Global's flash October composite PMI eased to 57.6 from a five-year high of 58.4 (in line with the 57.6 Econoday consensus); manufacturing 56.0 vs. 55.5 expected, services 57.9 vs. 58.0. The output-prices gauge jumped to 59.8, the highest since August 2022, and new orders hit 58.2, the highest since March 2022. University of Michigan (final October): sentiment 48.0 vs. 48.1 in September; 1-year inflation expectations 4.7% (from 4.6%) and long-run 3.5% (from 3.4%), both the highest since May; 69% of consumers expect rates to rise over the next year, the most since April 2023.
items.reason_en: Near term: hotter selling prices plus rising inflation expectations strengthen the case for a December hike – a headwind for gold. Longer term: with S&P Global's survey pointing to ~5% annualized Q4 growth, the Fed has no reason to pivot soon; gold only wins this one if inflation gets ahead of the Fed and real yields fall.

items.title_en: 10-year yield bounces 5 bps to 4.999% as crude tops $100 but still falls 11 bps on the week; S&P 500 hits a five-week low

Chris Rupkey of Fwdbonds said WTI closing above $100 means "more inflation is on the way," so yields are adjusting higher. items.reason_en: Near term: yields bouncing with crude was a direct headwind for gold on Friday. Longer term: the 10-year is well off its Oct. 5 high of 5.31% and down three weeks running – if the oil shock fades, a lower yield floor is what lets gold rebuild.

items.title_en: Odds of an Oct. 28 hike tick up to 10.3%; December still ~75% – Fed in blackout, Oct. 29 PCE is the next test
items.summary_en: Investing.com Fed Rate Monitor (based on CME 30-day fed funds futures, updated 8:25 PM ET Friday): Oct. 27–28 meeting – hold at 3.75%–4.00% 89.7%, 25 bp hike 10.3% (prior day 92.0% / 8.0%). Dec. 8–9 meeting – hold 24.9%, +25 bps 67.6%, +50 bps 7.5% (≈ 75% total odds of a hike). CNBC, citing CME FedWatch: 92% odds of no change next week and 78% odds of a December hike. The Fed is in its pre-meeting blackout, so no Fed speakers; the PCE report, the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, is due Oct. 29.
items.reason_en: Near term: a hold next week is all but priced, so the risk is the press-conference tone – a hawkish lean adds pressure on gold. Longer term: as long as December hike odds sit near 75%, gold lacks a durable bid; it takes a softer PCE and a pullback in those odds to give bulls a real opening.

items.title: Đặc phái viên Mỹ Tom Barrack: «Có thể có cuộc tấn công Iran ngay cuối tuần này» – Trump nói «không biết gì về việc đó»; Israel bầu cử 27/10
items.summary: AFP (qua The Hindu): Đại sứ Mỹ tại Thổ Nhĩ Kỳ Tom Barrack nói với podcast Mario Nawfal rằng Mỹ có thể tấn công Iran ngay cuối tuần này, dù ông không trực tiếp phụ trách hồ sơ Iran; ông cũng nói Mỹ không nhắm thay đổi chế độ. Khi được hỏi tại Florida, ông Trump đáp: nếu vậy thì «tôi không biết gì về việc đó». Trước đó ông Trump từng nói sẽ không tấn công trước bầu cử Quốc hội Mỹ 3/11. Thủ tướng Israel Netanyahu, đối mặt bầu cử thứ Ba 27/10, nhiều lần tuyên bố muốn lật đổ chính quyền Iran.
items.reason: Ngắn hạn: thị trường đóng cửa cuối tuần nên mọi diễn biến quân sự sẽ phản ánh vào giá mở cửa sáng thứ Hai (giờ VN) – có thể gây nhảy giá (gap) hai chiều: vàng được mua trú ẩn ban đầu, nhưng nếu dầu vọt thì cược Fed tăng lãi lại kéo vàng xuống như tuần này. Dài hạn: xung đột kéo dài giữ phần bù rủi ro địa chính trị cho vàng, nhưng tác động qua kênh dầu – lạm phát – lãi suất đang mạnh hơn.

items.title_en: US envoy Tom Barrack: an Iran strike "absolutely" could come this weekend – Trump says he "doesn't know anything about it"; Israel votes Oct. 27
items.summary_en: AFP (via The Hindu): Tom Barrack, US ambassador to Turkey, told podcast host Mario Nawfal the US could strike Iran as soon as this weekend, though he has no direct role on Iran; he also said Washington isn't seeking regime change. Asked in Florida, President Trump said, "If that's the case, I don't know anything about it." Trump had earlier said strikes would not come before the Nov. 3 midterms. Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu, facing an election Tuesday, Oct. 27, has repeatedly vowed to topple Iran's government.
items.reason_en: Near term: with markets shut, any weekend military action hits the Sunday-evening open (ET) – expect a gap either way: an initial haven bid, but if crude spikes, December hike bets can drag gold right back down like this week. Longer term: a drawn-out conflict keeps a geopolitical premium in gold, but the oil-inflation-rates channel is currently doing more of the work.
items.time_en: Oct 23, 6:43 PM ET (AFP report)

items.title_en: Gold heads for its worst week in more than four months (−3.5%) as oil keeps higher-for-longer in play; dip buyers defend 4,000
items.summary_en: CNBC (Reuters): spot gold eased 0.2% to $4,016.27 an ounce by 11:51 PM ET after touching its lowest since July 20 overnight (CNBC XAU= low 3,987.85). Gold is down 3.5% this week, on pace for its worst week since June; December futures fell 0.7% to $4,030.40. Capital.com says speculators are defending $4,000 because a clean break would mean the market has stopped pricing rate relief and started pricing sticky inflation, higher yields and a stronger dollar. Traders are looking ahead to next week's Fed meeting.
items.reason_en: Near term: 4,000 is the line – hold it and gold gets a technical bounce, but bounces keep getting sold while crude stays high. Longer term: as long as oil holds above $110 and a December hike stays on the table, reclaiming the 4,100–4,150 base is a tall order.

items.title_en: Brent climbs to $113.75–$114.40, on track for a third weekly gain as Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia continue; Aramco evacuates Dhahran HQ
items.summary_en: Reuters: Brent rose 0.5% to $113.75 a barrel and WTI 0.7% to $100.13 as of 12:39 AM ET; CNBC had Brent at $114.43 (+1.1%) and WTI at $100.85 by 2:45 AM ET. Brent is set for a third straight weekly gain. Saudi Aramco ordered the evacuation of its Dhahran headquarters as fighting with the Houthis intensified. ING says re-escalation looks like the most likely path, keeping a sizable geopolitical risk premium in crude. Libya cut output after a pipeline valve to Zawiya port was shut.
items.reason_en: Near term: more upside in crude weighs on gold through the inflation-to-Fed channel. Longer term: if the Gulf conflict spills into broader financial stress, haven demand could come back to gold.

items.title_en: Spot gold drops 2.8% to $4,024.55, lowest since July 20, as an oil spike and an AI sell-off push money into Treasuries instead of bullion
items.summary_en: Investing.com: spot gold settled Oct 22 at $4,024.55/oz (−2.8%), its lowest since July 20, while futures settled at $4,039.90 (−0.5%). It's the third break below $4,100 support this month. Trade Nation's David Morrison notes this week's selling came despite a sizable drop in the dollar, and daily MACDs haven't reached the oversold readings that usually fuel durable rallies. Peter Schiff: gold lost $116 and closed just above $4,000 support. CNBC's XAU= quote at 7:35 PM ET: $4,023.61 (day range 4,020.59–4,122.56).
items.reason_en: Near term: sellers own the tape below 4,100, and 4,000 is the line in the sand – lose it and the July lows come into play. Rallies into 4,100 look like selling opportunities. Friday brings flash PMIs at 9:45 AM ET and UMich sentiment at 10 AM ET. Longer term: as long as $110-plus Brent keeps a December hike priced, gold struggles to trade as a haven even with yields falling.

items.title_en: NYT: US and Israel draw up post-midterm strike plans on Iran; US orders staff out of Saudi Arabia – Brent settles at $113.17, highest since May 4
items.summary_en: CNBC: Brent rallied 4% to settle at $113.17 a barrel, its highest since May 4, while WTI gained 2.4% to $99.47 after briefly topping $100. The New York Times, citing US officials, reported that the US and Israeli militaries have specific plans for a "short but intensive" round of strikes on Iran after the Nov. 3 midterms. President Trump said Washington isn't negotiating with Tehran and something will happen "fairly soon." The State Department ordered non-emergency staff out of Saudi Arabia as Houthi attacks escalate; at least two people were killed at King Fahd International Airport in Dammam, and Saudi Aramco told staff to evacuate its Dhahran headquarters.
items.reason_en: Near term: this escalation is hurting gold, not helping it – the market is trading it through the oil-to-inflation-to-Fed channel rather than as a haven trigger. Longer term: the risk of direct strikes on Iran after Nov. 3 keeps crude elevated; if the conflict spills into broader financial stress, haven flows could rotate back into gold.

items.summary_en: Reuters (via Mint): the 10-year yield fell more than 17 bps to close at 4.972%, its biggest one-day drop since March 10, 2023 (it peaked at 5.3645% on Oct. 7); the 2-year dropped 18.5 bps to 4.638% and the 30-year sat at 5.287%. CNBC: the S&P 500 lost 1.2%, its worst day since July; the Nasdaq slid 2.6%, its worst since June; the Dow was flat. Meta fell about 7% after earnings and a new non-voting share class, and Nvidia dropped 4.4%. Cboe: the VIX briefly topped 20 before settling at 18.99.
items.reason_en: Near term: a big rally in Treasuries and gold still fell – haven money is choosing bonds, and the AI-driven de-risking is dragging other assets with it. Longer term: a 10-year back under 5% is constructive for gold once the oil shock cools; low claims say the labor market is still holding up.

items.title: Iran bác yêu cầu của Mỹ qua trung gian Pakistan: không đàm phán, không mở lại Hormuz khi Washington chưa đáp ứng điều kiện
items.summary: Reuters (qua Arab News): Iran báo với tư lệnh quân đội Pakistan Asim Munir sẽ không đàm phán với Washington cho tới khi 7 điều kiện mở lại eo Hormuz được đáp ứng – gồm dỡ phong tỏa cảng Iran, gỡ trừng phạt dầu, chấm dứt chiến sự trên mọi mặt trận; Thư ký Hội đồng An ninh Quốc gia Mohsen Rezaei nói toàn bộ uranium làm giàu sẽ ở lại Iran. Newsquawk: Ngoại trưởng Araghchi nói Mỹ «không có thiện chí» và ít lý do để kỳ vọng tiến triển; Mỹ công bố trừng phạt mới liên quan Iran nhưng cho dỡ hàng không phải gốc Iran trên một số tàu bị phong tỏa (ân hạn 30 ngày). Houthi nói đàm phán với Ả Rập Xê Út đã bế tắc.
items.reason: Ngắn hạn: tin hòa đàm hôm 20/10 đã bị dập tắt – phần bù rủi ro quay lại dầu, giữ lạm phát và lợi suất cao, nên vàng khó tận dụng được vai trò trú ẩn; tin chiến sự chỉ tạo nhịp giật 10–20 giá. Dài hạn: chỉ một thỏa thuận thật sự mở lại Hormuz mới hạ được dầu và kỳ vọng tăng lãi – đó là chất xúc tác tăng lớn nhất của vàng hiện nay.

items.title_en: Iran rebuffs U.S. demands via Pakistani mediators: no talks, no Hormuz reopening until Washington meets its conditions
items.summary_en: Reuters (via Arab News): Iran told Pakistan's army chief Asim Munir there will be no talks with Washington until its seven conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz are met – including an end to the U.S. port blockade, lifting oil sanctions and ending hostilities on all fronts; Supreme National Security Council secretary Mohsen Rezaei said all enriched uranium stays in Iran. Newsquawk: Foreign Minister Araghchi said the U.S. has shown no willingness to reach an understanding and there's little reason to expect progress. Washington rolled out new Iran-related sanctions while licensing the offload of non-Iranian cargo from some blocked vessels (a 30-day wind-down). The Houthis said talks with Saudi Arabia are deadlocked.
items.reason_en: Near term: Tuesday's peace-deal headlines are dead – the risk premium is back in crude, which keeps inflation and yields elevated, so gold can't cash in on its haven bid; war headlines are good for $10–20 spikes, not trends. Longer term: only a real deal that reopens Hormuz knocks oil and hike pricing down – that's the biggest bullish catalyst for gold right now.

items.title_en: A Qatar–Pakistan U.S.–Iran peace proposal sends gold up $22 to 4,153.50 – and the move fully unwinds after a diplomat says a deal isn't close
items.summary_en: The New Arab (Al-Araby Al-Jadeed): Qatar and Pakistan put a 'middle-ground' proposal to Iran and the U.S. – Iran would allow a confidential IAEA visit to its nuclear sites, and Washington would let Tehran collect interest on $6 billion in frozen funds held in Qatar; Pakistan's army chief Asim Munir delivered it in Tehran. Bloomberg: a diplomat involved in the talks said reports that a deal is close are inaccurate; gold swung between a 0.4% gain and a 0.7% loss. On CNBC's XAU= feed, spot ran from 4,130 to 4,153.50 in 15 minutes (10:15–10:30 AM ET), then settled back into 4,120–4,126. Meanwhile the IRGC said two tankers caught fire after hitting mines in the Strait of Hormuz, and Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia continued.
items.reason_en: Near term: peace headlines pull oil and yields lower and gold pops – but without confirmation the move fades fast, so stay flat for the first 15–30 minutes after a headline. Longer term: a real peace deal would cut crude and inflation expectations and take hike pressure off the Fed – that's the big bullish catalyst for gold; a drawn-out war keeps oil above $100 and yields high.

items.summary: Reuters (qua CNA): một tàu dầu nổ sau khi trúng thủy lôi ở phía nam eo Hormuz hôm Chủ nhật (theo IRGC); Kpler: dòng dầu thô vùng Vịnh tuần trước còn ~8,5 triệu thùng/ngày, từ hơn 20 triệu tuần trước đó, ít nhất 10 vụ tấn công tàu thương mại. SEB: Iran có thể leo thang trước bầu cử giữa kỳ Mỹ 3/11. Ả Rập Xê Út phát cảnh báo nguy hiểm ở Riyadh rồi gỡ bỏ; Houthi tấn công trại huấn luyện ở Shabwa (Yemen) làm 53 người chết. Ông Trump ký lệnh miễn trừ một số trừng phạt, thuế với hàng xuất khẩu Nga (thỏa thuận diesel với ông Putin). DTN: WTI tháng 11 chốt 103,66 (+2,22%), Brent tháng 12 chốt 109,55 (−0,3%, cao nhất phiên 110,70).
items.reason: Ngắn hạn: dầu cao giữ kỳ vọng lạm phát và lợi suất cao – bất lợi cho vàng qua kênh Fed, dù tin chiến sự nóng đôi lúc tạo nhịp mua trú ẩn 10–15 giá. Dài hạn: nếu Hormuz nghẽn kéo dài, lạm phát năng lượng buộc Fed giữ lập trường diều hâu – vàng khó bứt phá cho tới khi rủi ro chiến tranh chuyển thành rủi ro tăng trưởng.

items.title_en: Oil splits: expiring November WTI jumps 2.2% to $103.66 on Hormuz disruption, while Brent slips 0.3% to $109.55 on a 60-day Russia sanctions waiver
items.summary_en: Reuters (via CNA): an oil tanker exploded after hitting a naval mine in the southern Strait of Hormuz on Sunday, according to the IRGC; Kpler says Gulf crude flows fell to about 8.5 million barrels per day last week from more than 20 million the week before, with at least 10 confirmed incidents involving commercial vessels. SEB expects Iran to escalate further ahead of the Nov. 3 U.S. midterms. Saudi Arabia issued danger alerts for Riyadh before lifting them, and a Houthi attack on a training camp in Yemen's Shabwa province killed 53. President Trump signed an order waiving some sanctions and tariffs on Russian exports after a diesel deal with Putin. DTN: November WTI settled at $103.66 (+2.22%), December Brent at $109.55 (−0.3%, session high $110.70).
items.reason_en: Near term: high oil keeps inflation expectations and yields elevated – a headwind for gold through the Fed channel, even if war headlines spark $10–$15 haven pops. Longer term: a prolonged Hormuz squeeze forces the Fed to stay hawkish, and gold struggles to break out until war risk turns into growth risk.

items.title_en: Gold breaks $4,150 at the Wall Street open: money rotates back into AI stocks, the 10-year holds 5.10% – and a 29 NAHB print (31 expected) can't rescue it
items.summary_en: CNBC live blog (10:19 AM ET): the Nasdaq rose 1.4% and the S&P 500 0.7% as investors bought the dip in AI names after last week's rout; Intel gained 5% on a JPMorgan upgrade. Reuters (10:01 AM ET): the NAHB/Wells Fargo builder sentiment index fell three points to 29 in October – the lowest since June 2012, versus a 31 forecast – as 7.40% mortgage rates and war-driven materials costs hit demand; 43% of builders cut prices. Kitco: markets price about 89% odds of a December Fed hike and roughly 15% for the Oct. 27-28 meeting. CNBC spot gold: 4,159–4,166 around the open (9:25–9:35 AM ET bars) → 4,152.70 (9:40 bar) → 4,146.00 low (9:45 bar) → back to 4,154.40 just before NAHB (10:00 AM ET) → 4,149.30 (10:00 bar) → 4,144.45 (10:10 AM ET bar) → 4,143.45 low (10:15 AM ET bar); gold-api.com 4,149.60 at 10:20 AM ET. 10-year 5.108%, DXY 101.90 at 10:10 AM ET.
items.reason_en: Near term: no direct bad news – gold fell for lack of a reason to hold in a risk-on tape, and the break of the 4,159 London low tripped stops. A weak NAHB should have pulled yields lower, but the 10-year stayed at 5.10% – this market is trading inflation and the Fed, not housing. Longer term: as long as December hike odds sit near 89%, gold rallies are likely to get sold; softer jobs or inflation data is what would change the story.

items.title_en: Gold edges toward $4,190 in Asia as October hike odds fall below 20% – December still ~92%; gold ETFs log a 13th straight week of inflows
items.summary_en: Reuters (Sunday, 8:31 PM ET): spot gold was up 0.2% at $4,174.54/oz and December futures up 0.4% at $4,195.70. CME FedWatch puts the odds of an October hike at 16%, but a December hike at 92%. U.S. import prices rose more than expected in September on energy – more evidence inflation pressure is building. The IMF expects the ECB to hike by 25 bps at least once more this year. Bloomberg (updated 12:21 AM ET Monday): gold rose as much as 0.5% to near $4,190, erasing most of last week's loss, after traders read Chair Warsh's remarks as backing a hold next week; gold ETFs have added holdings for 13 straight weeks, though bullion is still down about a fifth since the U.S.-Iran war broke out in late February. CNBC spot (XAU=) at 2:50 AM ET: 4,178.30.
items.reason_en: Near term: fading October hike bets are why gold is holding above $4,160 – but with December still ~92% priced, it's hard to crack the $4,198–$4,208 lid without a fresh catalyst. Longer term: 13 straight weeks of ETF inflows say big money is still buying the dips, building a floor around $4,000–$4,100.

items.summary: CNBC: giá dầu giảm thứ Hai vì kỳ vọng nguồn cung Nga tăng sau khi Mỹ nới trừng phạt hôm thứ Sáu – ông Trump dùng quyền «lợi ích quốc gia» để hoãn thuế mới với các nước mua năng lượng Nga và gỡ trừng phạt xuất khẩu dầu diesel của Nga; Brent −1,8% về 107,88 USD, WTI −1,14% về 100,25. Giá CNBC lúc 13:43 VN: Brent 107,28 (−2,35%). CNBC Daily Open (08:16 VN): cuối tuần Ukraine phóng hơn 1.000 drone khắp nước Nga, kho và cảng dầu St. Petersburg bốc cháy; ông Zelensky gọi quyết định của Mỹ là «sai», Bộ trưởng Tài chính Bessent cảnh báo ông «cẩn trọng». Theo Newsquawk, ông Trump viết trên Truth Social rằng đàm phán hòa bình Nga–Ukraine đang «tiến triển đáng kể». Vùng Vịnh vẫn nóng: thứ Sáu thêm hai tàu chở dầu bị tấn công ngoài khơi Ả Rập Xê Út (UKMTO).
items.reason: Ngắn hạn: dầu hạ làm nỗi lo lạm phát và lợi suất dịu đi – đỡ vàng ở vùng 4.160–4.170; nhưng tin hòa bình làm giảm nhu cầu trú ẩn nên vàng khó bật mạnh. Dài hạn: nếu nguồn cung Nga quay lại thật sự, dầu và kỳ vọng tăng lãi cùng hạ – có lợi cho vàng; ngược lại tấn công ở Hormuz vẫn có thể đẩy Brent lên 110–120 bất cứ lúc nào.

items.title_en: Oil drops more than 2% to about $107 as Trump waives sanctions and tariffs on Russian energy and touts 'significant progress' on Ukraine – even after Kyiv's 1,000-drone weekend strike
items.summary_en: CNBC: crude fell Monday on expectations of more Russian supply after Friday's U.S. sanctions relief – President Trump invoked national interest to suspend new duties on buyers of Russian energy and lifted sanctions on Russian diesel exports. Brent fell 1.8% to $107.88 and WTI 1.14% to $100.25; CNBC quoted Brent at $107.28 (−2.35%) at 2:43 AM ET. CNBC Daily Open (Sunday, 9:16 PM ET): Ukraine launched more than 1,000 drones across Russia over the weekend, setting a St. Petersburg oil terminal and depot ablaze; Zelenskyy called the U.S. decision 'wrong,' and Treasury Secretary Bessent told him to 'be careful.' Per Newsquawk, Trump posted on Truth Social that Russia–Ukraine peace talks are making 'significant progress.' The Gulf is still hot: two more tankers were attacked off Saudi Arabia on Friday (UKMTO).
items.reason_en: Near term: cheaper oil cools inflation fears and yields, cushioning gold around $4,160–$4,170, but peace headlines drain the haven bid, so don't expect a big pop. Longer term: if Russian barrels really come back, oil and rate-hike expectations fall together – good for gold. A Hormuz attack can still send Brent back to $110–$120 at any moment.

items.reason_en: Near term: a soft euro keeps the dollar firm, so gold can't fully cash in on lower U.S. yields – one more reason it's stuck in a range. If French bond stress spreads, the haven bid could rotate back into gold. Longer term: both the Fed and ECB lean hawkish, and high real rates remain gold's main headwind.

items.summary_en: CNBC (Sunday, 10:05 PM ET): China's Q3 GDP grew 4.5% y/y (Q2: 4.3%, a three-year low; Reuters poll: 4.4%), putting nine-month growth at 4.6% – inside Beijing's 4.5%–5% target. items.title: Iran: Hormuz mở lại «vào ngày thứ 6» nếu Mỹ đáp ứng điều kiện; UKMTO: ít nhất 10 tàu bị tấn công trong tuần – Trump nói thỏa thuận sẽ đến sau bầu cử 3/11
items.summary: CBS News (Chủ nhật 18/10): Ngoại trưởng Iran Araghchi nói Tehran vẫn đang xem «góp ý» của Mỹ về đề xuất ngừng bắn 7 ngày từ tháng 9 (Mỹ dỡ phong tỏa cảng Iran, gỡ trừng phạt dầu, ngừng bắn trên mọi mặt trận); nếu Mỹ đáp ứng, Hormuz mở lại vào ngày thứ 6 và đàm phán bắt đầu ngày thứ 7. UKMTO: ít nhất 10 tàu bị tấn công trong hoặc gần Hormuz kể từ Chủ nhật tuần trước – cao nhất một tuần kể từ khi chiến tranh nổ ra tháng 2 – và 23 vụ từ đầu tháng. Al Jazeera: Trump nói không dùng vũ khí hạt nhân, không đưa quân bộ vào Iran và tin thỏa thuận chấm dứt chiến tranh sẽ đạt được sau bầu cử giữa kỳ 3/11.
items.reason: Ngắn hạn: tín hiệu ngoại giao có nhưng chưa có gì ràng buộc, trong khi số vụ tấn công tàu lại tăng – rủi ro tin bất ngờ hai chiều, vàng dễ giật mạnh theo tiêu đề. Dài hạn: kịch bản hòa bình (dầu rẻ, lạm phát hạ, Fed bớt tăng lãi) là kịch bản tích cực nhất cho vàng theo nhiều chuyên gia; mốc thời gian sau 3/11 cần theo dõi.

items.title_en: Iran says Hormuz could reopen 'on the sixth day' if the US meets its terms; UKMTO counts at least 10 ships attacked in a week – Trump eyes a deal after Nov. 3
items.summary_en: CBS News (Sunday): Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Tehran is still reviewing US "comments" on its seven-day ceasefire proposal from September, which calls for lifting the US blockade of Iranian ports, removing oil sanctions and a ceasefire on all fronts; if Washington complies, Hormuz reopens on day six and talks begin on day seven. UKMTO says at least 10 vessels have been attacked in or near the strait since last Sunday, a weekly high since the war began in February, with 23 attacks so far this month. Per Al Jazeera, President Trump ruled out nuclear weapons and ground troops and said he expects a deal to end the war after the Nov. 3 midterms.
items.reason_en: Near term: there's a diplomatic opening, but nothing binding, while ship attacks are rising, so headline risk cuts both ways and gold can whip around on the news. Longer term: a peace deal, meaning cheaper oil, cooler inflation and fewer Fed hikes, is the most bullish setup for gold, and the post-Nov. 3 window is worth watching.

items.title: Warsh tại IMF Bangkok: 'Tôi không đoán trước các cuộc họp' – không phát tín hiệu tăng lãi tháng 10, USD về đáy gần 2 tuần
items.summary: CNBC: trong buổi trò chuyện với Tổng Giám đốc IMF Kristalina Georgieva (10:30 VN), Chủ tịch Fed Kevin Warsh không cho biết Fed có tăng lãi tiếp trong tháng này hay không: 'Tôi không đoán trước các cuộc họp. Tôi không tin vào việc nói bây giờ mình sẽ làm gì ở các cuộc họp còn lại trong năm' – nhắc lại quan điểm phản đối định hướng chính sách (forward guidance). Ông nói các NHTW đang 'thắt chặt đồng loạt' trên toàn cầu nên 'không có ai được hưởng lợi miễn phí', và khẳng định Fed sẽ đưa giá cả về ổn định. Đây là lần phát biểu cuối trước giai đoạn im lặng từ thứ Bảy, trước cuộc họp 27–28/10. FXStreet: USD bị bán trở lại, vàng hút lực mua từ vùng 4.150.
items.reason: Ngắn hạn: không có tín hiệu diều hâu mới → thị trường gần như loại trừ việc tăng lãi tháng 10, USD yếu đi và vàng được đỡ. Nhưng Warsh cũng không loại trừ tăng lãi, nên từ giờ đến 28/10 dữ liệu Mỹ sẽ quyết định – vàng dễ giật mạnh theo từng con số. Dài hạn: Fed bỏ forward guidance làm biến động quanh mỗi cuộc họp lớn hơn; xu hướng thắt chặt đồng loạt toàn cầu vẫn là gió ngược với vàng.

items.title_en: Warsh at the IMF in Bangkok: 'I don't prejudge meetings' – no October hike signal, dollar slides to a near two-week low
items.summary_en: CNBC: in a fireside chat with IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva, Fed Chair Kevin Warsh declined to say whether the Fed will hike again this month: 'I don't prejudge meetings. I don't believe in saying now what I might do at the meetings that we have in the balance of this year,' reiterating his opposition to forward guidance. He described a 'synchronous tightening' by central banks worldwide, meaning 'there's no free riders,' and said the Fed will deliver price stability. These were his last public remarks before the blackout starts Saturday ahead of the Oct 27–28 FOMC. FXStreet: the dollar came under fresh selling and gold drew dip buyers from the $4,150 area.
items.reason_en: Near term: no new hawkish signal, so the street is close to pricing out an October hike; a weaker dollar supports gold. But Warsh didn't rule a hike out either, so the data between now and Oct 28 calls the shots, and gold will swing hard on every print. Longer term: a Fed without forward guidance means bigger moves around each meeting, and synchronized global tightening remains a headwind for bullion.

items.reason_en: Near term: a wider conflict footprint (Hormuz, Yemen, Saudi Arabia) keeps haven demand alive, but it also props up the dollar, which limits the lift; Trump ruling out nukes and ground troops trims the extreme-escalation tail. Longer term: without a US–Iran deal, geopolitical risk stays a floor under gold, even though rates are the dominant driver right now.

items.title_en: India: major fund houses halt new money into gold ETF funds from Oct 16 after a SEBI nudge – right before Diwali
items.summary_en: Reuters (via The Hindu BusinessLine): Kotak, UTI, HDFC and other large Indian fund houses issued notices late Thursday suspending bulk subscriptions to gold ETFs while still allowing redemptions; sources said the move followed a nudge from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI). CNBC TV18: from Oct 16, ICICI Prudential, HDFC, Aditya Birla, Invesco, DSP, Tata and others stopped taking fresh money into gold ETF fund-of-funds (lump sums, new SIPs, top-ups); existing SIPs and redemptions continue, and the ETFs still trade on exchange. India's September gold imports fell to $1.8 billion from $2.3 billion in August. Times of India: FoFs account for about a third of roughly ₹1.7 lakh crore in gold ETF assets, and industry officials don't see it as a game changer for demand.
items.reason_en: Near term: a sign that India, the world's No. 2 gold consumer, wants to curb imports right into festival season dents seasonal demand expectations – a mild negative. Longer term: if curbs widen (import duty is already 15%), Indian physical demand could stay soft; but FoFs are small, so this isn't a trend-setter on its own.

items.title_en: Dollar backs off an 18-month high: DXY −0.45% to 101.99, euro posts its best day in nearly two months – a tailwind for gold
items.summary_en: Reuters (4:48 PM ET): the dollar index fell 0.45% to 101.99 after hitting an 18-month high on Wednesday; the euro rose 0.56% to $1.1218, sterling gained 0.64% to $1.3275, the yen firmed 0.15% to 158.08 per dollar, and the Aussie lost 0.77% after a surprise drop in Australian employment. The bond rally and cautious Fed remarks (Bowman, Daly) cooled October hike bets; CME FedWatch (per Reuters) showed a 73% chance of a hold at the Oct. 27–28 meeting, up from 53% a month ago. Monex USA's Juan Perez said the market has turned 'anti-USD' after four weeks of heavy dollar gains.
items.reason_en: Near term: a weaker dollar makes bullion cheaper for non-U.S. buyers, which supports price. Longer term: most major brokerages still see one more Fed hike in December (Reuters), so the dollar can regain its footing if inflation stays hot – a risk for gold.

items.summary: Gulf News (cập nhật 06:31 VN 16/10): Tư lệnh quân đội Iran Amir Hatami nói eo Hormuz 'đã đóng, vẫn đóng' cho tới khi quyền lợi của Iran được tôn trọng; CENTCOM bác bỏ, nói Mỹ và đối tác kiểm soát eo biển, hơn 40 tàu thương mại đi qua trong 24 giờ trước đó và có ngày hơn 19 triệu thùng dầu thô được đưa qua. Euronews (23:00 VN 15/10): một tàu dầu chưa rõ tên bốc cháy ở Vịnh Oman khi đi vào vùng Iran cấm, sự cố thứ hai trong 24 giờ, sau khi GFS Pride và Cape Dao bị chìm. CNN (qua Gulf News): Mỹ đang tính khả năng dùng bom GBU-43/B (MOAB) nhắm hạ tầng năng lượng và cơ sở hạt nhân Iran nếu ông Trump quyết định nối lại chiến sự. Bộ trưởng Tài chính Bessent công bố trừng phạt mới với mạng lưới tài chính của Iran: 'vòng thòng lọng đang siết lại'. Houthi bắn tên lửa vào dinh tổng thống ở Aden (Yemen).
items.reason: Ngắn hạn: nguy cơ Mỹ nối lại tấn công Iran và các vụ tấn công tàu liên tục giữ cầu trú ẩn → hỗ trợ vàng khi có tin bất ngờ; nhưng đồng thời đẩy giá dầu và kỳ vọng lạm phát, kìm vàng qua kênh lãi suất. items.title_en: Iran says Hormuz 'remains closed' as CENTCOM counts 40-plus transits in 24 hours; another tanker burns in the Gulf of Oman – CNN: U.S. weighs MOAB
items.summary_en: Gulf News (live, through 7:31 PM ET): Iran's army chief Maj. Gen. Amir Hatami said the Strait of Hormuz 'remains closed' until Iran's rights are respected; CENTCOM pushed back, saying U.S. and partner forces control the strait, more than 40 commercial vessels transited in the prior 24 hours and over 19 million barrels of crude moved through in a single day. Euronews (12:00 PM ET): an unnamed tanker caught fire in the Gulf of Oman after entering an Iranian-declared prohibited zone, the second such incident in 24 hours, following the sinking of GFS Pride and Cape Dao. CNN (via Gulf News) reported the U.S. is planning for possible use of the GBU-43/B MOAB against Iranian energy and nuclear sites if President Trump renews combat. Treasury Secretary Bessent announced new sanctions on Iran-linked financial networks, saying 'the noose is tightening.' Houthi missiles also targeted the presidential palace in Aden, Yemen.
items.reason_en: Near term: the risk of renewed U.S. strikes on Iran and nonstop shipping attacks keep haven demand alive, which helps gold most when headlines hit by surprise; the same shocks lift crude and inflation expectations, which works against gold through rates. Longer term: a drawn-out, widening conflict (Saudi Arabia vs. the Houthis) keeps a floor under haven and central bank demand.

items.title_en: Crude splits at the settle: WTI jumps 3% to $97.97 on an 8.6M-barrel U.S. stock draw, Brent slips to $105.92 (−0.13%)
items.summary_en: Reuters: Brent settled down 14 cents (−0.13%) at $105.92 a barrel, while WTI rose $2.88 (+3.03%) to $97.97. The EIA said U.S. crude stocks fell 8.6 million barrels to 415.6 million in the week ended Oct. 9, versus a 288,000-barrel draw expected in a Reuters poll. Brent was held back as Washington weighs easing sanctions on 'shadow fleet' tankers so legal oil can move on previously sanctioned vessels; the IEA agreed to release more than 20 million barrels of diesel as soon as possible, and Spain will tap 4.4 million barrels of reserves in October. Shipping attacks around Hormuz and the Saudi–Houthi conflict keep a geopolitical premium in the market.
items.reason_en: Near term: Brent above $100 keeps energy inflation alive and supports Fed hike bets, neutral to slightly negative for gold; supply steps (IEA, sanctions relief) take some heat out. Longer term: if supply loosens, gasoline and diesel could cool into the Nov. 3 midterms, easing rate pressure and helping gold; a fresh Gulf strike would reverse that quickly.

items.title_en: Hormuz heats up: Singapore-flagged boxship sunk, IRGC 'counting the moments' to hit U.S. warships – reports Iran is evacuating bases
items.summary_en: CNBC Daily Open (9:35 PM ET Oct 14): the Singapore-registered container ship GFS Pride was hit by an unidentified projectile, caught fire and sank in the Strait of Hormuz; all 21 crew were evacuated safely. A second vessel, GFS Giselle, took hull damage but reached safe anchorage. Singapore's maritime authority called the attacks a breach of international law. Tehran said it is 'counting the moments' until it can strike U.S. warships, while CENTCOM said U.S. and partner forces clearly control the strait. investingLive (8:40 PM ET Oct 14): unconfirmed reports say the IRGC ordered several military bases evacuated, and Iranian officials reportedly told regional diplomats they are '100% certain' a U.S. strike is coming.
items.reason_en: Near term: rising U.S.–Iran escalation risk supports haven demand, especially if the evacuation reports are confirmed or a strike actually lands. The oil channel cuts the other way by feeding inflation and Fed hike bets, so gold benefits most when war headlines hit as a surprise. Longer term: a drawn-out conflict (the IMF now assumes Hormuz reopens only in March 2027) keeps a floor under haven and central bank demand.

She said gasoline is driving headline inflation while core remains sticky, upside inflation risks stay elevated, and a stable labor market lets the Fed focus on prices. Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee called the CPI data discouraging, and the Beige Book flagged intensifying, diesel-driven price pressure. Investing.com notes Chair Kevin Warsh speaks late Thursday New York time at the IMF meetings in Bangkok, before the Fed's blackout begins Saturday.
items.reason_en: Near term: Daly takes some air out of an October hike (a small plus for gold) but confirms the tightening bias, firming up a December move – a net negative. Warsh is the next big event risk after PPI and retail sales. Longer term: 'higher for longer' keeps real yields positive, the main headwind for bullion.

items.title_en: Houthi missile hits Saudi Aramco HQ building in Dhahran after Saudi strikes on Sanaa – Brent edges up to ~$106.40 in Asia
items.summary_en: Reuters: Saudi Arabia's Energy Ministry confirmed an Aramco administrative building in Dhahran was hit Tuesday evening (Saudi time), causing a limited fire and no casualties. A company source said a ballistic missile struck the office tower, damaging the top three floors. Earlier, the Saudi-led coalition hit the Sabah fuel depot outside Sanaa, Yemen; the Houthis threatened both Aramco's headquarters and a Riyadh refinery. Debris from an intercepted missile injured four people in Riyadh. President Trump spoke with Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman; the US has not joined the fighting directly. Iran has kept the Strait of Hormuz closed since February, which makes the Bab el-Mandeb route even more important. Markets: Brent (BZ=F, Yahoo) $106.39 at 7:45 PM ET Oct 13 vs. a $105.69 settle; COMEX gold (GC=F) flat around $4,179–4,184 (6:00–7:45 PM ET). No CNBC story on the Aramco attack yet.
items.reason_en: Near term: geopolitical risk is a safe-haven tailwind for gold, but the bigger effect runs through oil – higher crude → hotter inflation → more reason for the Fed to hike → firmer dollar and yields → headwind for gold. The two forces offset, so gold barely moved overnight. Bigger picture: if the Houthis keep hitting Saudi oil infrastructure, crude can spike and pull rate-hike bets higher; if the US or Turkey gets drawn in and the war escalates, the safe-haven bid for gold should become clearer.

items.summary: FXStreet (18:21 GMT 13/10 = 01:21 VN 14/10): Chủ tịch Fed New York John Williams nói các lực giảm lạm phát vẫn đang vận hành, thị trường lao động không góp phần đẩy lạm phát, áp lực giá chủ yếu từ AI và năng lượng; 'thêm một lần tăng lãi suất trong năm nay là phù hợp' và hiện không thấy cần tăng năm 2027. Cùng ngày, Thống đốc Christopher Waller (Reuters, 06:57 EDT 13/10 = 17:57 VN) nói lợi suất trái phiếu tăng là do tăng trưởng thực, đầu tư AI và lo ngại nợ công, không phải do kỳ vọng lạm phát – vốn vẫn 'neo vững'. USD: chỉ số DXY trên CNBC 102,215 (−0,36%), biên độ ngày 102,162–102,574, lùi khỏi đỉnh 18 tháng. Vàng COMEX GC=F (Yahoo, nến 5 phút): 01:00 VN 4.174,5 → 01:05 4.182,1 → 01:55 4.186,5 → 02:30 4.188,8.
items.reason: Ngắn hạn: thông điệp 'chỉ còn một lần tăng rồi dừng' khiến USD hạ nhiệt, vàng COMEX bật khoảng 10–14 USD trong 1,5 giờ sau đó. Trung – dài hạn: nếu Fed xác nhận đỉnh lãi suất ở 4,00–4,25% và không tăng tiếp năm 2027, áp lực lãi suất lên vàng sẽ giảm dần; tuy nhiên Collins và Hammack vẫn diều hâu, nên CPI tối nay mới là phép thử.

items.title_en: Fed's Williams (NY Fed, voter): one more hike this year is appropriate, no need seen for 2027 – DXY slips to ~102.2
items.summary_en: FXStreet (2:21 PM ET Oct 13): New York Fed President John Williams said disinflationary forces are still at work, the labor market isn't adding to inflation, and price pressure is coming mainly from AI and energy; 'one more rate increase this year is appropriate' and he currently sees no need to hike in 2027. The same day, Governor Christopher Waller (Reuters, 6:57 AM ET) said rising Treasury yields reflect real growth, AI investment and debt concerns – not inflation expectations, which remain 'well anchored'. Dollar: DXY on CNBC 102.215 (−0.36%), day range 102.162–102.574, backing off an 18-month high. COMEX gold (GC=F, Yahoo, 5-min bars): 2:00 PM ET 4,174.5 → 2:05 PM 4,182.1 → 2:55 PM 4,186.5 → 3:30 PM 4,188.8.
items.reason_en: Near term: a 'one more and done' message cooled the dollar and COMEX gold bounced about $10–14 over the next 90 minutes. Bigger picture: if the Fed confirms a terminal rate of 4.00–4.25% with no hikes in 2027, rate pressure on gold should fade over time; but Collins and Hammack are still hawkish, so today's CPI is the real test.

items.title: Kazakhstan chuyển từ mua sang bán vàng: giảm tỷ trọng vàng trong dự trữ từ 78% xuống 75% trước cuối 2026
items.summary: Bloomberg (qua Oninvest) và Kitco (đăng 15:37 UTC 13/10 = 22:37 VN): Phó Thống đốc NHTW Kazakhstan Aliya Moldabekova nói lợi suất trái phiếu Mỹ cao nhất 24 năm khiến USD hấp dẫn hơn và giảm sức hút của vàng; vàng đã chiếm khoảng 78% dự trữ ngoại hối (386 tấn, dự trữ 66,4 tỷ USD cuối tháng 9), 'giống danh mục một tài sản'. Mục tiêu giảm về 75% trước cuối năm, một nửa bằng bán quyền chọn và một nửa bán vàng vật chất (báo Kazakhstan ước khoảng 12 tấn, ~1,6 tỷ USD). Nếu vàng dưới 4.000 USD, tỷ trọng có thể tự giảm về mục tiêu.
items.reason: Ngắn hạn: tin xấu về tâm lý vì NHTW mua vàng là trụ cột của đà tăng nhiều năm; khối lượng ~12 tấn không lớn nhưng tạo nguồn cung bán quanh vùng giá hiện tại. Trung – dài hạn: nếu thêm NHTW khác tái cân bằng khi lợi suất Mỹ cao, lực đỡ từ cầu chính phủ yếu đi; ngược lại Trung Quốc vẫn mua 23 tháng liên tiếp, nên chưa phải xu hướng chung. Mốc 4.000 USD là vùng cần theo dõi.

items.title_en: Kazakhstan flips from buyer to seller: cutting gold to 75% of reserves from 78% by end-2026
items.summary_en: Bloomberg (via Oninvest) and Kitco (posted 11:37 AM ET Oct 13): Kazakhstan central bank Deputy Governor Aliya Moldabekova said 24-year-high Treasury yields make the dollar more attractive and gold less so; gold already makes up about 78% of FX reserves (386 tonnes, $66.4B in reserves at end-September) – 'like a single-asset portfolio'. The target is 75% by year-end, half via selling options and half via physical sales (local press estimates roughly 12 tonnes, ~$1.6B). If gold drops below $4,000, the share could fall to target on its own.
items.reason_en: Near term: bad for sentiment, since central-bank buying has been a pillar of the multi-year rally; ~12 tonnes isn't large, but it adds supply around current prices. Bigger picture: if other central banks rebalance while US yields are high, official-sector support weakens; on the other hand China has bought 23 months in a row, so it's not a broad trend yet. $4,000 is the level to watch.

items.title: Fed Collins (Boston): sẽ cần tăng lãi thêm trước cuối 2026 – vàng COMEX tụt ~5 USD về quanh 4.181 sau phát biểu
items.summary: Chủ tịch Fed Boston Susan Collins phát biểu 4:00–4:45 chiều ET 13/10 (= 03:00–03:45 giờ VN 14/10) tại hội nghị ngân hàng khu vực Boston Fed. Reuters (16:01 ET): bà ủng hộ đợt tăng lãi tháng 9 lên 3,75–4,00% và hiện cho rằng 'sẽ phù hợp nếu tăng lãi thêm một chút trước cuối năm để đảm bảo lạm phát quay về mục tiêu 2% một cách kịp thời và bền vững'. Thời điểm hành động phụ thuộc dữ liệu tới. Bà lạc quan về tăng trưởng GDP và thị trường lao động gần toàn dụng, nhưng cảnh báo lạm phát tổng và lõi sẽ lại trên 2% vài tháng tới vì giá nhiên liệu tinh chế (jet, diesel, dầu sưởi), đầu tư AI, thuế quan và chiến tranh Trung Đông. CNBC chưa có bài cùng ngày; chưa thấy bản phát biểu đầy đủ trên trang Boston Fed. Phản ứng vàng (COMEX GC=F, Yahoo, nến 5 phút): 00:00 4.176,1 · 02:00 4.185,9 · 02:30 4.188,8 · 03:00 (bắt đầu) 4.186,2 · 03:15 4.183,0 · 03:20 chạm 4.180,7 · 03:30 4.180,8 · 03:40 4.181,2. Spot gold-api.com 4.160,3 USD lúc ~03:51 VN. DXY 102,19 (02:30) → 102,20 (03:00) → 102,21 (03:40). Lợi suất 10 năm (^TNX) dừng quanh 5,217% lúc 01:55 VN (phiên trái phiếu Mỹ đã hẹp).
items.reason: Giọng diều hâu rõ: Collins xác nhận còn một lần tăng lãi trước cuối 2026 (thị trường đang nghiêng về tháng 12 hơn là họp 27–28/10). Theo lý thuyết, Fed còn thắt chặt + lợi suất cao bất lợi vàng ngắn hạn — thực tế GC=F giảm khoảng 5–8 USD (4.186 → ~4.181) trong 20–40 phút sau giờ mở màn. Dài hạn: nếu CPI 19:30 VN tối 14/10 nóng, xác suất tăng lãi tháng 12 tăng và vàng dễ tiếp tục chịu áp lực; nếu CPI dịu, bài của Collins ít tác động hơn vì bà không bỏ phiếu năm nay.
